title: Breakfast grace
hookLine: a short blessing turns a meal into thanksgiving
tomorrow: can the drive to school be a pilgrimage?

cards: Phones come out before forks. The plate gets its photo before anyone takes a bite. There's an older pause at that same moment, and it isn't for anyone's feed.

One familiar Catholic grace asks God to bless us and these gifts we're about to receive from his bounty, through Christ our Lord. A few seconds over a bowl of cereal. So why stop at all, when the food is right there?

teach.b: Because in this tradition, thanks comes first, before the food is even tasted.
Paul gives the reason in his first letter to Timothy: "every creature of God is good, and nothing to be rejected that is received with thanksgiving." Received with thanksgiving: that's the hinge.
The same food, received as a gift instead of grabbed. The Gospels show Jesus doing it.

teach.h: HE GAVE THANKS, THEN BROKE IT.
teach.b: He takes bread, gives thanks, then breaks it, for crowds on a hillside and at the Last Supper.

And here's one to tell a friend over breakfast: the Catechism says the word Eucharist comes from the Greek for giving thanks. So a morning grace is a small cousin of the Mass: bread, thanks, then eating.
The words can be the familiar grace, one sentence of your own, or the sign of the cross over a bowl.
Look at the week's mornings together: a first thought turned to God, the whole day offered, water at the sink, and now a pause at the table. Ordinary holiness, so far, takes about a minute.

how: Catholic families often say a short grace before meals, such as 'Bless us, O Lord, and these thy gifts', with the sign of the cross; some also give thanks after eating.

o: the first meal after a day of fasting
a short blessing of thanks before eating
a blessing a priest says over a kitchen

p: from the Greek for giving thanks

s: grace before meals has to be a long, formal prayer
one sentence of thanks, or a sign of the cross over a bowl, is grace too.
the word Eucharist comes from the Greek for giving thanks
the Catechism says so: the Mass is an action of thanksgiving.

games.q: at a friend's house, her family dives straight into dinner without grace. you usually pause first. what fits today's idea?
o: give thanks quietly, maybe a small sign of the cross, then eat.
ask everyone to stop and pray together before anybody eats.
skip it this once; grace only counts when the whole table says it.
games.why: grace is thanks first, not a performance. a silent thanks keeps the pause without asking anyone else to share it.

practice: If you have something to eat or drink nearby, take one bite or one sip, slowly, and taste it all the way through before you swallow.
Before the next, pause for one breath of thanks, to God if you pray, or to everyone whose hands it passed through on its way to you.

wordCard.voice: Breakfast grace. A short blessing before the first bite that turns a meal into thanks.

orig.note: Greek: having given thanks. what Jesus does over bread before he breaks it.

carryVoice: Your line: thanks first. Before the photo, before the fork, before the first bite. Enjoy your breakfast.
